benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
benchmarks.what: A combined score from nine evaluations covering knowledge work, coding, science and general knowledge, run by Artificial Analysis on each model.
benchmarks.caveat: Cost per task is Artificial Analysis's weighted average API cost per Index task.
benchmarks.updated: Index v5.0.1; board shows no update date, retrieved Nov 11, 2026

benchmarks.name: Arena Text
benchmarks.what: Human preference: people compare two anonymous answers to their own prompts and pick the better one. Ratings on an Elo-like scale; style control adjusts for answer length and formatting.
benchmarks.caveat: Neighbouring models often have overlapping confidence intervals; see the ± range in each model's details.

benchmarks.name: Epoch Capabilities Index
benchmarks.what: Epoch AI's single capability score, combining results from many benchmarks.

benchmarks.name: Vals Index
benchmarks.what: Agentic tasks in finance, law, tax and software, weighted by each sector's share of US GDP, run by Vals AI.
benchmarks.caveat: Cost per task is Vals's published cost per test.

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index
benchmarks.what: Models run inside coding-agent tools on three evaluations: FrontierCode, SWE-Atlas QnA and Terminal-Bench v4. The tool used is shown with each score; several are the developer's own tool.
benchmarks.caveat: Cost per task is Artificial Analysis's average API cost per task.
benchmarks.updated: board shows no update date, retrieved Nov 11, 2026

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 4.1
benchmarks.what: Tasks carried out in a computer terminal, run inside named agent tools. Share of trials solved.
benchmarks.caveat: Cost here is derived: the board's total cost divided by its number of trials (cost per trial). The board does not say which results it verified.
benchmarks.updated: latest result Sep 29, 2026, board retrieved Nov 11, 2026

benchmarks.name: Arena WebDev
benchmarks.what: Human preference for web apps the models build from a prompt, judged side by side.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench Coding
benchmarks.what: LiveBench's coding suite, scored automatically from 0 to 100.
benchmarks.caveat: A single run of 24 tasks per model, so a difference of a few points can be one task. Cost here is derived: LiveBench's total suite cost divided by its task count, as the LiveBench site itself does.

benchmarks.name: Arena Agent
benchmarks.what: Real agent sessions on arena.ai: how much better each model does than a baseline at finishing users' multi-step tasks, from task outcomes and user feedback.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench Browser
benchmarks.what: LiveBench's browser-agent suite: tasks completed by operating a web browser, scored from 0 to 100.
benchmarks.caveat: A single run of 25 tasks per model, so a difference of a few points can be one task. Cost here is derived: LiveBench's total suite cost divided by its task count, as the LiveBench site itself does.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench Research
benchmarks.what: LiveBench's research suite, scored from 0 to 100.
benchmarks.caveat: A single run of 22 tasks per model, so a difference of a few points can be one task. Cost here is derived: LiveBench's total suite cost divided by its task count, as the LiveBench site itself does.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench Long Agentic
benchmarks.what: LiveBench's long agentic suite: long, multi-step agent tasks, scored from 0 to 100.
benchmarks.caveat: A single run of 18 tasks per model, so a difference of a few points can be one task. Cost here is derived: LiveBench's total suite cost divided by its task count, as the LiveBench site itself does.

benchmarks.name: Vending-Bench 2
benchmarks.what: A simulated year running a vending-machine business: ordering stock, setting prices, dealing with suppliers. Score is the money left at the end (start: $500).
benchmarks.caveat: Cost per task is the mean API cost of one full simulated year.
benchmarks.updated: board shows no update date, retrieved Nov 11, 2026

benchmarks.name: LiveBench Data Analysis
benchmarks.what: LiveBench's data-analysis suite, scored from 0 to 100.
benchmarks.caveat: A single run of 150 tasks per model, so a difference of a few points can be one task. Cost here is derived: LiveBench's total suite cost divided by its task count, as the LiveBench site itself does.

benchmarks.name: Arena Vision
benchmarks.what: Human preference on prompts that include images, such as charts, photos and screenshots.

benchmarks.name: Vectara Hallucination Rate
benchmarks.what: How often a model adds facts that are not in a document it is asked to summarise. Lower is better.

benchmarks.name: FrontierMath (Tiers 1-3)
benchmarks.what: Unpublished, expert-written research-level maths problems, run by Epoch AI.

benchmarks.name: GPQA Diamond
benchmarks.what: Graduate-level multiple-choice questions in biology, chemistry and physics, run by Epoch AI.
benchmarks.caveat: Top models are close to the ceiling, so small gaps mean little.

benchmarks.name: ARC-AGI-2
benchmarks.what: Visual grid puzzles where each task needs a new rule to be worked out, run by the ARC Prize Foundation.
benchmarks.caveat: Cost per task is ARC Prize's measured cost per task.

groups.name: Coding agents
groups.desc: Agents that read a codebase, write and test changes, and work in the terminal, as in Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.

groups.name: Web and app builders
groups.desc: Tools that turn a description into a working web page or small app, judged by the people who asked for it.

groups.name: Browser and computer use
groups.desc: Agents that operate a browser for you: navigating sites, filling forms and pulling information out.

groups.name: Research agents
groups.desc: Agents that search, read many sources and pull the findings together into a cited answer.

groups.name: Long-running autonomous agents
groups.desc: Agents trusted with a goal over a long period, making many decisions without a person checking each one.

groups.name: Business and knowledge work
groups.desc: Finance, legal, tax and analysis tasks of the kind office teams hand to an AI assistant.

groups.name: Documents and data analysis
groups.desc: Working with spreadsheets, tables, reports and images of documents, and staying faithful to the source.

groups.name: Everyday assistant and chat
groups.desc: Drafting, explaining and answering questions in conversation: what most staff use AI for day to day.

groups.name: Hard reasoning, maths and science
groups.desc: Problems that need long, careful reasoning: engineering calculations, proofs and technical analysis.

method_steps: Four research agents read each benchmark's own leaderboard or data file and each developer's model and price pages. Every value was copied as published, with the address it came from.

Rankings use the results each benchmark publishes on its own board. Scores that developers report about their own models in announcements or model cards are not used. Some boards accept submitted runs; their notes say so.

Benchmarks spell model names differently. Each name is matched to one entry. Earlier snapshots, previews, quantised builds and products not sold through the API are kept apart. When a model appears at several reasoning-effort settings, it is ranked on its best setting, which is shown with the score.

Two further agents that did not collect the data re-checked values against the source pages and challenged the name matches, prices, costs and wording. Errors they found are fixed, or the value is removed, before publication.
disclaimer: Benchmarks measure narrow tasks under one set of conditions, and results move quickly as models and agent tools change. Gaps of a few points are often within the margin of error. A model that ranks first here may not be the best on your own documents, processes or data. List prices change and some are introductory; open-weight prices depend on the host. Several well-known boards are not used to rank: SWE-bench, SWE-Bench Pro, OSWorld, tau-bench, BFCL and Aider have results for few or none of the models listed here, and METR's time-horizon board is no longer updated. This page is general information, not purchasing advice. Chmltech has no commercial relationship with any model developer or benchmark listed.
